title: How to build world-class AI products — Sarah Sachs (AI lead @ Notion) &  Carlos Esteban (Braintrust)
talk_summary: Sarah Sachs (Notion AI) describes running AI product quality through observability plus evals, spending ~90% of effort on evals rather than prompting, using per-sample LLM-judge prompts, deterministic/heuristic scorers, and a model-swap regression loop. The Braintrust workshop then shows the mechanics: task+dataset+scorer evals in UI and SDK/CI, production logging with online scoring, human-in-the-loop annotation, and remote evals for complex local tasks.

takeaways.technique: Per-sample rule-based LLM-judge prompts instead of one generic judge
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of one prompt judging the whole dataset ('is this concise/faithful'), they write a specific judge prompt per dataset row stating the exact rules the output must satisfy (language, format, must-cite page A), which keeps golden sets current as the index changes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for every single element in your data set or trace... you have a particular prompt... we actually just say like what are the rules for what we want

takeaways.what_they_do: They pair LLM judges with exact code checks: e.g. every tool call in a Jira dataset must have 'Jira' in its query; a multilingual dataset asserts output language; a markdown-format scorer is binary 0/1.
takeaways.evidence_quote: everything in that data set that tool call should have in its query must be Jira... we can also make deterministic functions

takeaways.technique: One-button model-swap regression suite per prompt
takeaways.what_they_do: Because prompts are modular per task, when a new cheap/fast model ships they gather the high-frequency use cases, run all evals on them in one click, see which prompts it passes, and switch only those prompts.

takeaways.technique: Summarize failures with an LLM into a report for the engineer
takeaways.what_they_do: They take failing samples, pass them to another LLM to summarize the biggest themes/deltas, and write a short report so the engineer sees what to fix instead of reading thousands of samples.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we actually will take the failures and pass them into another LLM and ask them to summarize what the failures are so that we can write a quick report

takeaways.technique: Evals as ad-hoc CI gate on curated regression datasets
takeaways.what_they_do: For certain experiences they run curated eval datasets before shipping (not full CI because evals are slow), and they keep datasets of known-hard cases (multilingual switching) to prevent regressions.

takeaways.technique: Per-span scoring to localize where a multi-step pipeline failed
takeaways.what_they_do: In a multi-step app they score individual spans (e.g. the question-rephrase step) not just the final output, so when output is wrong they can see which step broke.
